scenario.name: Symbiote Parasitic Linux LD_PRELOAD Rootkit & libpcap eBPF Bytecode Hooking
scenario.overview: Imagine a parasitic mist that refuses to walk down a bank hallway as a visible stranger and instead weaves itself into the master uniform coatroom. Every clerk, courier, and auditor who puts on an official jacket automatically wears the parasite too: inside couriers it silently copies every vault passphrase spoken at the counter, and inside safety auditors it clouds their magnifying lenses so the spy own hidden tunnels vanish from every inspection log. In this scenario (T1574.006, Symbiote Parasitic Linux LD_PRELOAD Rootkit & libpcap eBPF Bytecode Hooking), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: global Dynamic Linker Injection (e.g., /usr/lib/liblinux.so), then pAM Backdoor Authentication (so the next stage can build on pam backdoor authentication), then libpcap Function Hooking (..., SO_ATTACH_FILTER). Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Global Dynamic Linker Injection (e.g., /usr/lib/liblinux.so), then PAM Backdoor Authentication (so the next stage can build on pam backdoor authentication), then libpcap Function Hooking (..., SO_ATTACH_FILTER). Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 1 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: Global Dynamic Linker Injection via /etc/ld.so.preload
stages.subtitle: Persistence & Privilege Escalation (T1574.006 - Dynamic Linker Hijacking)
stages.description: Rather than hiring a separate intruder who would show up on the employee attendance sheet, the spy hangs a rigged lining inside the building universal uniform rack. From that second forward, every single worker who clocks in slips the hidden parasite onto their own sleeves automatically. Rather than running as a separate process, Symbiote was deployed as a shared library (e.g., /usr/lib/liblinux.so) and added to /etc/ld.so.preload (a system-wide configuration file read by the GNU dynamic linker /lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2 that forces the specified .so library to be mapped into the address space of every dynamically linked process before libc.so.6), allowing Symbiote to override standard library functions (fopen, readdir, getdents64, execve) via symbol interposition. If an administrator runs cat /etc/ld.so.preload, ls /usr/lib, or ldd /bin/ls using standard dynamically linked system binaries, Symbiote’s hooked fopen and getdents64 functions filter out its own filenames and return empty/clean results. In the documented EDR exchange from Symbiote DNS / HTTPS C2 Operator to Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap, Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap responds with ALERT T1574.006 (confirming that the Stage 1: Global Dynamic Linker Injection via /etc/ld.so.preload request succeeded on Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap and establishing the runtime state required for Step #2 Stage 2: PAM Backdoor Authentication & ssh/scp libc_read Keystroke Harvesting). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ Stage 1: Global Dynamic Linker Injection via /etc/ld.so.preload / ⇠#1 ALERT T1574.006) from Node ① (#1 Symbiote DNS / HTTPS C2 Operator) to Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Hooked tcpdump / libpcap BPF Scrubber).

stages.title: Stage 2: PAM Backdoor Authentication & ssh/scp libc_read Keystroke Harvesting
stages.subtitle: Credential Access & Persistence (T1556.003 - Pluggable Authentication Modules)
stages.description: Riding inside the sleeves of every courier and gate clerk, the parasite silently transcribes every vault combination typed at the dispatch desk into a locked notebook, while secretly installing a master override phrase that lets the spy walk through the front gate under any clerk name. When loaded inside ssh or scp client processes, Symbiote hooked libc’s read() function to capture administrator passwords and keystrokes into an RC4-encrypted stash file (/var/tmp/.certs). When loaded inside the sshd daemon, it hooked pam_authenticate() and pam_acct_mgmt() (granting instant root SSH login whenever the attacker authenticated with a hardcoded master password, while scrubbing /var/log/auth.log and utmp/wtmp). Harvesting outbound ssh and scp credentials from compromised jump boxes allowed the attackers to pivot laterally across segmented banking infrastructure. In the documented Auth exchange from Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap to /etc/ld.so.preload (liblinux.so), /etc/ld.so.preload (liblinux.so) responds with ACK T1556.003 (confirming that the Stage 2: PAM Backdoor Authentication & ssh/scp libc_read Keystroke Harvesting request succeeded on /etc/ld.so.preload (liblinux.so) and establishing the runtime state required for Step #3 Stage 3: libpcap Function Hooking & Kernel BPF Bytecode Scrubbing Against tcpdump). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ Stage 2: PAM Backdoor Authentication & ssh/scp libc_read Keystroke Harvesting / ⇠#2 ACK T1556.003) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 /etc/ld.so.preload (liblinux.so)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Hooked tcpdump / libpcap BPF Scrubber).

stages.title: Stage 3: libpcap Function Hooking & Kernel BPF Bytecode Scrubbing Against tcpdump
stages.subtitle: Defense Evasion (T1014 - Rootkit / Network Capture Blindfolding)
stages.description: Whenever building inspectors raise a magnifying glass to watch outgoing mail trucks for smuggling, the parasite riding inside the inspector own glasses silently swaps in tinted lenses that blot out the spy truck license plates before the report even reaches the page. To defeat live network forensics on the infected host, Symbiote hooked pcap_compile() in libpcap and setsockopt(..., SO_ATTACH_FILTER...) in libc. Whenever an analyst ran tcpdump or tshark, Symbiote intercepted the compiled Berkeley Packet Filter (BPF) bytecode array before it was handed to the kernel and prepended its own BPF instructions (which instructed the Linux kernel to silently drop any packet matching Symbiote’s C2 ports or DNS tunneling domain before copying packets to tcpdump). Symbiote also hooked fopen("/proc/net/tcp") and removed lines matching its active connections so netstat and ss could not see its sockets either. In the documented EDR exchange from /etc/ld.so.preload (liblinux.so) to Hooked sshd / PAM Credential Harvester, Hooked sshd / PAM Credential Harvester responds with ALERT T1014 (confirming that the Stage 3: libpcap Function Hooking & Kernel BPF Bytecode Scrubbing Against tcpdump request succeeded on Hooked sshd / PAM Credential Harvester and completing the final execution objective of Symbiote Parasitic Linux LD_PRELOAD Rootkit & libpcap eBPF Bytecode Hooking). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ Stage 3: libpcap Function Hooking & Kernel BPF Bytecode Scrubbing Against tcpdump / ⇠#3 ALERT T1014) from Node ③ (#3 /etc/ld.so.preload (liblinux.so)) to Node ④ (#4 Hooked sshd / PAM Credential Harvester), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Hooked tcpdump / libpcap BPF Scrubber).
